title: Humiliation of Christ
definition: The humiliation of Christ refers to the Son's willing lowliness in His incarnation, obedience, suffering, and death for sinners.
summary: Jesus humbled Himself to save His people.
christFocus: Christ's humiliation displays divine love, servant-hearted obedience, and the mercy of God toward sinners.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The humiliation of Christ does not mean He ceased to be God or lost divine glory in His nature. It means the eternal Son willingly took the form of a servant, entered human weakness, obeyed under the law, suffered, and died.

This humiliation reveals the depth of divine love. The Lord of glory did not grasp at status but stooped to rescue sinners.

Christ's path of humility becomes the pattern for His people. Those who belong to Him are called to humble service rather than self-exaltation.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Pride wants a glorious Christ without a humble cross. The humiliation of Christ matters because salvation came through lowliness, suffering, and obedience.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Follow Christ in humility. Serve without demanding recognition, and remember that your Savior came low to lift sinners by grace.
